resolution: Building pieces now get the same live procedural face-skins as props. The hard difference: prop meshes are individual nodes (so a re-skin hid the stale baked node), but building-piece boxes are BATCHED instanced draws and can't be hidden per-instance. So instead of hiding, the live skinned face-slab is rendered as a textured cube OUTSET ~8mm to sit just proud of the baked face and cleanly occlude it (no z-fight, no batch surgery). Baseline-free like the prop skin fix, so it covers existing pieces and survives hot reloads. JS buildingSkinBoxes decomposes pieces via pieceVisualShapes; a skinned face-slab carries textureKey 'bldskin:<id>' which resolves to a procedural shader → emit a 32-byte box (transform + matHash) + material. Host door __compiled_world_set_live_skin_boxes; world_loader.appendLiveSkinBoxes renders each as a one-instance textured cube into a pre-sized per-frame buffer outset by SKIN_BOX_OUTSET, reusing the live-material path; applyLiveMeshProps restructured so skin boxes render even with no mesh props in the scene. Shipped clean, committed bac3b1bc4. Slice scope: procedural skins, box faces (skinned ramps deferred). The OUTSET (8mm) is a one-constant tweak if skins look proud of the surface. Flat colors + image decals for both props and pieces are the next follow-up ('images for both').
